editorial.headline: Communication Repair: Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans the repair and maintenance of communication equipment, with a clear national opening to foreign investment and an equally clear Bali restriction.
editorial.body:
Communication equipment repair is a broad, practical technical activity: restoring and maintaining the devices and systems that move information between people, networks and places. Its scope reaches from wireless telecommunications equipment—mobile phones, RFID devices, tablets, handheld computers, wireless modems and vehicle trackers—to wired equipment such as fax machines, analogue telephones, ADSL/HDSL equipment, PABX systems, modems, routers and bridges.

It also covers repair work on cable-based transmission equipment, including analogue telephone exchanges; radio-transmission equipment such as microwave links, studio-to-transmitter links and troposcatter links; and two-way radio systems, from trunking and conventional radio communications to walkie-talkies. The activity extends further to radio transmitters and receivers: broadcast television transmitters, television and smart-TV sets, broadcast radios, mobile-network transmitting and receiving equipment, and video cameras. In other words, this is an activity defined by the upkeep of communications infrastructure and the devices at its edges, rather than by one narrow class of hardware.

The national position is direct. The activity is open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. It is available across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the record does not confine the work to a specialist workshop, a particular network technology or a single level of enterprise; it frames the activity as a repair-and-maintenance field available from micro through large business scale.

Bali changes the registration picture for PMA entirely. At present in Bali, a foreign investor is unable to register this activity. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is classified as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, bringing the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The restriction has applied under the Bali moratorium since May 2026. The national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling remains the national rule, but it does not override Bali’s PMA registration block for this activity.
